old_caption: The video captures a mechanical press in action, applying pressure to a vibrant, textured object. The press, marked with yellow and black hazard stripes, descends onto a circular metallic base. Beneath the base lies a colorful, spiky sphere composed of alternating layers of purple and pink. As the press compresses the sphere, it deforms under the force, causing the spikes to flatten and the colors to blend slightly. The background is a plain green wall with some visible wear and tear, adding an industrial feel to the scene. The camera remains stationary throughout, focusing on the interaction between the press and the sphere, highlighting the transformation of the object's shape and texture as the pressure increases.

caption: The video captures a vertical press assembly centered against a green wall marked with two yellow warning signs. A cylindrical head wrapped in yellow-and-black diagonal stripes sits atop a polished circular metal plate, while a matching lower plate rests on the workbench. Between the plates lies a pink-and-purple spiky ball, its ridged disc shape compressing as the upper assembly descends. As the clip progresses the upper plate moves downward while the lower plate stays fixed, narrowing the gap and squeezing the ball. The ball's height shrinks and it bulges outward, spreading wider than the lower plate's diameter while its spiky ridges remain visible. Near the final frames the descent and deformation slow, leaving the ball as a thin compressed layer still held between the plates.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
